title: VAT remittance posting briefly blocks checkout

brief.headline: both guardians agree the decision belongs to a human
brief.what_broke: No lock waits: no session is blocked.
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 55% over 30s (60/132 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $8,364/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

brief.recommendation: Checkout at 55% success (BIZ-4) vs 95% SLO, $8,364/min revenue at risk, ~30s left in 60s tolerance window (BIZ-1). The vat_remittance_post workload is PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT, never_interrupt, non-replayable (BIZ-2). No active lock contention (DB-3) and no protected settlements in flight (DB-2). Root cause is application-layer (pool saturation, client timeouts, downstream deps) outside database authority. Tax & Treasury team must decide on mitigations.

audit.report: The vat_remittance_post job (pid 1483261, PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT class, never_interrupt policy) was idle in transaction for 4.2s and briefly blocked checkout. Checkout degraded from 90% success (5 timeouts in 15s) to 55% success over 30s (60/132 failed), putting $8,364/min revenue at risk with ~30s remaining in the 60s business tolerance window. The database guardian initially proposed waiting, but after confirming the blocker was no longer locking (DB-3) while checkout remained at 55% success, both guardians agreed to escalate to human on-call. No action was executed; the negotiation took 205.5s.
audit.root_cause: The vat_remittance_post job (PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT, never_interrupt) was idle in transaction, briefly blocked checkout, and checkout remained degraded at 55% success even after lock contention cleared.
audit.negotiation_critique: Database guardian reasonably proposed WAIT initially (4.2s blocker age, 90% checkout success) then switched to ESCALATE after discovering checkout collapsed to 55% and the blocker was PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT/never_interrupt; continuity guardian accepted without objection. Both correctly honored the never_interrupt invariant. However, the 205.5s negotiation duration exceeded the 60s business tolerance window.
follow_ups: Investigate why vat_remittance_post was idle in transaction (missing commit/rollback in application code?).
Determine why checkout remained degraded at 55% after lock contention resolved (connection pool exhaustion? cascade failure?).
Review whether never_interrupt policy for vat_remittance_post is appropriate given its business impact during incidents.

events.title: R1 after investigating: switches to escalate

proposal.rationale: DB-3 confirms no lock waits currently — the blocking session from DB-1 (pid 1483261, vat_remittance_post) is no longer blocking. However, checkout success has collapsed to 55% over 30s (BIZ-4), with $8,364/min revenue at risk and only ~30s remaining in the 60s business tolerance window (BIZ-1, BIZ-4). The vat_remittance_post workload is class PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT, replayable=False, policy never_interrupt (BIZ-2), so termination is policy-prohibited even if it were still blocking. Since the database lock contention has resolved but checkout remains severely degraded, the root cause is likely application-level (connection pool exhaustion, client-side timeouts, etc.) and outside database guardian authority. Escalation to the owning team with a decision brief is required.
proposal.expected_effect: Human owners receive a brief: no active lock contention (DB-3), checkout at 55% success and worsening (BIZ-4), blocker workload is protected and non-interruptible (BIZ-2), ~30s left in business tolerance window. They can investigate application-layer causes (pool saturation, client timeouts, downstream dependencies) and decide on mitigations (e.g., circuit breakers, scaling, shedding load).
proposal.risk_assessment: Escalation consumes time (~seconds) but avoids policy violation (never_interrupt) and futile termination of a non-blocking session. Risk is that checkout continues to degrade during handoff; however, no database action can improve checkout now (no locks held).
changes: Switched from wait to escalate because DB-3 shows the lock contention has resolved but checkout failure persists and worsens (BIZ-4), indicating a non-database root cause. The blocker workload is protected and cannot be terminated per policy (BIZ-2). Waiting would waste the remaining tolerance window without addressing the actual problem.
